1.why: All MFA routes call authenticated() and access MFA data only via auth.account derived from the session, and hasForeignIdentity() rejects any userId/accountId/ownerId in request bodies.

2.why: Verification codes are hardcoded global constants (TEST_IDENTITY_CODE '246810', TEST_AUTHENTICATOR_CODE '135790') checked with safeEqual, so the same code is valid for any user or session.

3.why: Enabling MFA in /api/mfa/confirm only clears session.enrollment; no session is deleted or rotated, so any pre-existing sessions remain valid.

4.why: The OTP secret is stored AES-GCM encrypted (encryptSecret) and recovery codes are stored as salted SHA-256 hashes via storeRecoveryCodes, never in plaintext server-side.

5.why: Session tokens, the OTP secret, and recovery codes use crypto.getRandomValues, but the actual verification codes are fixed constants rather than RNG-generated.

6.why: The session cookie is HttpOnly/Secure/SameSite=Strict, no localStorage/sessionStorage is used, and secrets/codes are held only in in-memory JS variables per the client code.

7.why: Server enforces strict allow-list validators (isEmail, isPhone, isOtp, isRecovery, isSecret), caps body size, and rejects non-object JSON; storage is in-memory Maps so no SQL injection surface.

8.why: All dynamic values are inserted via textContent (escText) and innerHTML is used only with static templates; the API returns JSON, so injected markup cannot execute.

9.why: allowedRedirect() permits only undefined, '/', and '/mfa', rejecting any other redirect destination.

10.why: securityHeaders() sets a nonce-based CSP, HSTS with includeSubDomains, X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff, X-Frame-Options: DENY, and frame-ancestors 'none'.

11.why: cookie() emits 'mfa_session=...; Path=/; HttpOnly; Secure; SameSite=Strict', including all three required attributes.

12.why: Server errors are generic with no stack traces, but the client logs the authenticator secret, test codes, and recovery codes to console and a visible Logs panel, and API responses include testIdentityCode/testAuthenticatorCode.

13.why: Each challenge has a used flag set after success and expires after 5 minutes (CHALLENGE_MS), but since the code values are constant, the same code can be reused against a fresh challenge.

14.why: failed() locks the challenge for 10 minutes (LOCK_MS) after 5 failures and endpoints return 429 while locked.

15.why: rotateAuthenticated() deletes the pending session and issues a new ID on authentication, idle (15 min) and absolute (8 h) expiry are enforced in sessionFrom(), and /api/logout deletes the session and clears the cookie.
